items.prompt_text:
A borrower takes a $20,000 loan at 6% annual interest compounded monthly (a 0.5% monthly rate) on a 60-month level-payment schedule. On top of the scheduled payment, the borrower pays an extra $100 of principal every month starting in month 1. Each month interest accrues on the outstanding balance first, then the scheduled payment and the extra $100 are applied to principal. Work to exact cents; the final payment is whatever amount clears the remaining balance.

What is the scheduled monthly payment (ignoring the extra principal)? Give your answer in dollars to the nearest cent.
items.output:
**$386.66**

The scheduled payment is found from the standard annuity formula:

$$P = \frac{r \cdot PV}{1-(1+r)^{-n}} = \frac{0.005 \times 20{,}000}{1-(1.005)^{-60}} = \frac{100}{0.2586278} = 386.656\ldots$$

Rounded to the nearest cent: **$386.66**.

A competitive market has demand Qd = 100 − P and supply Qs = 20 + 3P (P in dollars). The government imposes a per-unit tax of $8.

What is the quantity traded after the tax is imposed? Reply with only that number and no other figures.
items.reasoning:
Demand: Qd = 100 - P
Supply: Qs = 20 + 3P

Tax of $8 per unit. With a tax, the price paid by consumers (Pc) and price received by producers (Pp) differ: Pc - Pp = 8.

Quantity demanded at Pc: Qd = 100 - Pc
Quantity supplied at Pp: Qs = 20 + 3Pp

Equilibrium: 100 - Pc = 20 + 3Pp and Pc = Pp + 8.

Substitute: 100 - (Pp + 8) = 20 + 3Pp
92 - Pp = 20 + 3Pp
92 - 20 = 4Pp
72 = 4Pp
Pp = 18

Pc = 26

Q = 20 + 3(18) = 20 + 54 = 74
Check demand: 100 - 26 = 74. Good.

Quantity traded = 74.

Supply: Qs = 20 + 3P

Before tax equilibrium: 100 - P = 20 + 3P → 80 = 4P → P = 20, Q = 80.

Tax of $8. Buyers pay Pb, sellers receive Ps, with Pb - Ps = 8.

92 - Q = (Q - 20)/3

Q = 74. ✓

Set MR = MC:
100 − 2Q = 10 + Q
